title: Add VPC control plane Terraform module: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Add a reusable Terraform module and supporting defaults to provision the VPC control plane used by Redwood Private installations. This includes multi-AZ public/private subnet layout, interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/ECR/STS, security group templates for control-plane-to-worker and control-plane-to-internal services, cross-account VPC peering bootstrap helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone peering records. The goal is to provide an operator-friendly, auditable module that plugs into the private-installer and the Terraform-based deployment flow.

What this PR does (summary):
- New module: modules/vpc-control-plane with inputs for AZs, cidr blocks, subnet sizing, endpoint toggles, and tagging policy.
- Subnet resources: creates multi-AZ private and management subnets with NAT and route table associations (configurable).
- Interface endpoints: optional creation of interface endpoints for com.amazonaws.* services needed by on-prem control plane (SSM, EC2, ECR, STS, KMS).
- Security groups: control-plane and worker SGs with least-privilege defaults and documented ports.
- Peering helpers: cross-account peering resource templates and an outputs map suitable for automated acceptance by Route53 peering association module.
- Route53: private hosted zone peering association resources + examples for namespace delegation and glue records.
- Integration: wiring and examples for private-installer and the terraform/installer pipeline, with an upgrade hook to safely add endpoints to existing VPCs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module with examples and variables file
- [x] Unit tests (terraform validate / tflint configs)
- [x] Integration example in /examples/private-installer/vpc-control-plane
- [x] Upgrade hook script and doc for rolling changes with zero downtime
- [x] Docs: README, variables explanation, and security considerations

Backward compatibility: Module uses opt-in toggles for interface endpoints and peering to avoid accidental changes during upgrades. Upgrade hook performs a plan-only dry run and requires operator confirmation for peering and DNS changes.

Risks/Notes:
- Route53 peering across accounts requires acceptance from the remote account; the module emits the expected rfq output but does not automatically accept cross-account associations.
- Some cloud providers have soft limits on interface endpoints per AZ; docs include guidance and an optional batching setting.

How to test: follow examples in examples/private-installer/ with the provided terragrunt wrapper and apply to a sandbox account. The integration test uses a mock peering acceptor to validate outputs in CI.

Related: references previous VPC control plane PR series (pr-918273, pr-894321) and the private-installer docs update (docs#installer-vpc).

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can we make the interface endpoint creation opt-in by default? Some customers hit soft limits and we should avoid accidental creates during upgrades.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Good call — switched endpoints to disabled by default and added batching/limit variables. Also added migration docs in upgrade-hooks/README.
Marina Alvarez (reviewer): SG rules look permissive on the control-plane -> worker SG; can we tighten CIDR ranges and document when to open additional ports?

Aisha Kapoor (author): tightened defaults to only allow control-plane CIDR for worker ports and added a variables map for service-specific CIDR overrides. Added security considerations section in README.
Sven Eriksson (reviewer): Route53 cross-account flow needs clearer operator steps. Suggest emitting an output artifact with the expected association payload.
Aisha Kapoor (author): added route53_association_payload output and example acceptance command in docs.
release_notes: Add reusable VPC control-plane Terraform module that supports multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SG templates, cross-account peering helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone associations. Opt-in endpoints and peering to avoid accidental changes during upgrades.
notes_for_ops: When upgrading an existing control plane: run modules/vpc-control-plane/upgrade-hooks/plan-and-apply.sh against a staging environment to preview endpoint and peering changes. Peering requires remote account acceptance; coordinate with the peer owners before applying. Monitor CloudWatch for ENI creation limits per AZ.
egress_summary: Default SG allows HTTPS (443) outbound to service endpoints; KMS and ECR endpoints are created as interface endpoints when enabled. NAT gateway usage is opt-in via variable to support air-gapped installs.
changelog_entry: terraform(vpc-control-plane): new module to provision multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering helpers, and Route53 peering associations (A.Kapoor)
security_impact: Low: module follows least-privilege defaults and requires explicit opt-in for cross-account peering and interface endpoints. Operators must verify IAM policies used by peering acceptors.
testing_instructions: Follow examples/private-installer/README.md to provision into a sandbox account. Use the terragrunt wrapper to run 'terragrunt plan' and then 'terragrunt apply' with the --auto-approve flag only after manual verification of the plan. The CI integration uses a mocked peering acceptor to validate outputs.
